## Exp-3 analysis (generated by `eval/exp3.py` from `results/exp3_preds/`)

n = 200 golden utterances per condition, one speaker, one session, rotor noise (DREGON, evaluation partition), mixed on active-speech level. Artefact `qwen2.5-0.5b-instruct-Q4_K_M` under `schema/cmd.gbnf`, whisper `tiny.en` with the domain prompt, Silero endpointing at 450 ms.

### Provenance

The `text` condition (reference transcripts through the runtime parser) reproduces Surface B's per-item raw output on all 200 items: EM here is Table 17's EM.

### Pre-registered: arcsine-transformed CRR, one-way ANOVA + Tukey HSD across SNR

F(4, 995) = 5.47, p = 0.00023.

| A | B | CRR A - B | Tukey p |
| :--- | :--- | ---: | ---: |
| clean | 20 dB | +0.015 | 0.998 |
| clean | 15 dB | +0.040 | 0.921 |
| clean | 10 dB | +0.100 | 0.2306 |
| clean | 5 dB | +0.195 | 0.00053 |
| 20 dB | 15 dB | +0.025 | 0.9854 |
| 20 dB | 10 dB | +0.085 | 0.3942 |
| 20 dB | 5 dB | +0.180 | 0.0018 |
| 15 dB | 10 dB | +0.060 | 0.724 |
| 15 dB | 5 dB | +0.155 | 0.0115 |
| 10 dB | 5 dB | +0.095 | 0.2797 |

Two properties of this test must travel with it. (1) The unit is the utterance, whose outcome is 0 or 1, and arcsin(sqrt(x)) maps {0, 1} to {0, pi/2}: on binary data the transform is a rescaling and changes nothing. (2) The same 200 utterances appear in every condition, so the groups are not independent, which one-way ANOVA assumes. The paired test below is the one whose assumptions hold; it is reported beside the pre-registered one, not instead of it.

### Paired: Cochran's Q across the five conditions, McNemar per pair

Q = 56.65, df = 4, p = 1.5e-11. Pairwise McNemar, Bonferroni over 10 pairs (alpha = 0.0050); exact binomial below 25 discordant pairs, Edwards' continuity-corrected chi-square (`chi2_cc`) from there up.

| A | B | b (A only) | c (B only) | test | p | signif. |
| :--- | :--- | ---: | ---: | :--- | ---: | :--- |
| clean | 20 dB | 8 | 5 | exact | 0.5811 | no |
| clean | 15 dB | 15 | 7 | exact | 0.1338 | no |
| clean | 10 dB | 31 | 11 | chi2_cc | 0.0034 | yes |
| clean | 5 dB | 47 | 8 | chi2_cc | 3e-07 | yes |
| 20 dB | 15 dB | 8 | 3 | exact | 0.2266 | no |
| 20 dB | 10 dB | 25 | 8 | chi2_cc | 0.0053 | no |
| 20 dB | 5 dB | 46 | 10 | chi2_cc | 2.9e-06 | yes |
| 15 dB | 10 dB | 20 | 8 | chi2_cc | 0.0376 | no |
| 15 dB | 5 dB | 40 | 9 | chi2_cc | 1.8e-05 | yes |
| 10 dB | 5 dB | 34 | 15 | chi2_cc | 0.0101 | no |

### Operational envelope

| Threshold | lowest SNR meeting it (point) | lowest SNR meeting it (95% CI lower bound) |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| CRR >= 0.80 (NFR-7's level) | none (clean misses) | none (clean misses) |
| CRR >= 0.65 (NFR-8's level) | 15 dB | none (clean misses) |

The envelope is contiguous from clean downward: it ends at the first tested level that misses, even if a lower level happens to meet the threshold.

| clean | 23 | 0 | 0 | 0.690 | 0.730 |

| 10 dB | 21 | 0 | 0 | 0.590 | 0.620 |

Where the failures come from. A failed single-segment item is an ASR or parser error on a whole utterance; a failed split item may also be the endpointer handing the parser a fragment.

Reference text (the `text` condition): 13 of 200 failed, of which safe 0 (dispatched: formation 1, move 1, rotate 11).

### Error analysis: one cause per failed item

Causes are assigned in the order of the columns (`eval/exp3.py:CAUSES`), so every failure is counted once. 'ASR error' means the transcript differs from the reference after `eval/norm.py` normalisation.

| Condition | failed | parser wrong on reference text | no segment | split by endpointer | perfect transcript, parser wrong | ASR error, wrong intent | ASR error, right intent, wrong slot |
| :--- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| clean | 62 | 12 | 0 | 22 | 0 | 5 | 23 |
| 20 dB | 65 | 12 | 0 | 22 | 1 | 4 | 26 |
| 15 dB | 70 | 12 | 0 | 21 | 1 | 7 | 29 |
| 10 dB | 82 | 12 | 0 | 20 | 1 | 19 | 30 |
| 5 dB | 101 | 12 | 0 | 16 | 0 | 21 | 52 |

CRR of record is 'every segment': a split utterance is recognised only if every command it dispatched was correct. Items with no segment dispatched nothing and are counted as safe failures.
